findings.reason: §6 would name `cocos_convention.py` as the raw-side owner and drive it with a JT-60SA sign table, rather than generalising the DIII-D challenge scorer for a job a generalised owner already does.
findings.text: §6 identifies the source COCOS from "the sign products that the Sauter and Medvedev coefficients constrain" read from plasma shots, and cites only `challenge/convention.py measure_diiid_convention` as reusable, proposing to "generalise the entry point to take an equilibrium record through a loader"; but `data/cocos_convention.py` already owns exactly that computation, with `score_convention`/`score_conventions`/`surviving_conventions` parameterised by `observations: Sequence[ShotSignObservation]` (the MAST table is only the default) and `format_sign_report` emitting the sign report §6's done-when names — so §6 risks writing a second source-COCOS scorer instead of supplying JT-60SA `ShotSignObservation` rows to the existing one

findings.reason: the loader boundary §6 proposes must be stated as a record contract (canonical keys) so that `_integrated_current` is genuinely reusable, otherwise it is a rewrite dressed as a loader.
findings.text: the plan's §6 says "the reusable part is its Grad–Shafranov current integral, `_integrated_current`" of `challenge/convention.py`, but `_integrated_current` (line 245) and `_axis_and_boundary` (line 225) read DIII-D corpus keys (`efit_grid_R`, `efit_psirz`, `efit_z_axis`, …) directly, so a SELENE/FAME loader cannot reach them without either a key-renaming record contract or a rewrite; the plan does not say which

findings.reason: §7 must name the extension to the verdict's field set (q95, Ip, whitened magnetics residual) or name the second owner for the residual metric, rather than implying judge_geometry already covers the done-when's quantities.
findings.text: §7 states `judge_geometry` "already scores model geometry against an injected reference equilibrium into a `GeometryVerdict` (boundary RMS, axis position, q), so §7 adds a SELENE reference loader and its firewall tier to it instead of a parallel comparator"; but `GeometryVerdict` (line 174) carries only `axis_error`, `xpoint_error`, `boundary_rms`, `n_boundary_points`, `components`, `passed` and `notes` — there is no q, no Ip and no whitened magnetics residual, and the module contains no residual or global-quantity scoring; §7's done-when requires all three per shot, so the comparator change is materially larger than the "loader and firewall tier" the plan names

findings.reason: the author must state whether store format/root/probe-angle source become declared catalogue slots (and under which justification) or stay function parameters, because resolution from the catalogue today has no home.
findings.text: §4 says the store format, root and probe-angle source are "resolved from the catalogue rather than from the machine name", but `MachineMapCatalog` (machine_map.py:947) has no store-format, store-root or probe-angle-source field and `load_machine_map` uses `_exact_keys` over a fixed required set (machine_map.py:1084), so §4 necessarily adds catalogue/schema slots for machine addressing; §2's done-when only justifies new slots that carry "a JT-60SA structure, such as a SELENE-deck conductor element", which does not cover machine-addressing fields, so the plan's own slot criterion excludes the slots §4 needs

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each new surface is one function hiding the transport and layout (the §3 extractor is "one batch-fetch function and one cache writer"; the §2 exporter is one function; the §7 EQDB reader reuses the extractor's transport and cache), so no shallow-wrapper spread.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 names `eval/efit_referee.py` `judge_geometry` as the comparator owner but its `GeometryVerdict` scores only axis, xpoint and boundary_rms; q95, Ip and the whitened magnetics residual the §7 done-when requires have no owner named.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — each section that adds surface states what it retires or why nothing can be: §2 exporter "retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §3 extractor "retires nothing, because ambix has no remote reader today"; §4 retires the `machine == "mast"` branch; §7 EQDB reader "retires nothing, because no equilibrium-database reader exists in ambix". (public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 this week.)
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §6 searches `challenge/convention.py` for source-COCOS identification but misses `data/cocos_convention.py`, whose `score_convention`/`surviving_conventions` already generalise over a `ShotSignObservation` cohort, defaulting only to `MAST_LEVEL2_SIGN_TABLE`.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the §3 extractor is a parallel implementation rather than a wrapper, and the section names codex's `remote/scripts/enumerate_edas.py` remote layer and states why it is not imported (it would make imas-codex a dependency of every ambix read), with the shared-core decision deferred to a second facility.
